submission.natural_language_explanation: Fires on the word that closes a short clause or noun phrase naming the matter under discussion, above all the gap-final word of an embedded wh- or relative clause about a problem ("where the problem is", "what your plan is", "what is going on", "the thing I'm missing", "doing something wrong", "how to fix it") and abstract discourse nouns after a determiner ("confirm this observation", "these assertions", "the idea", "in mind"), plus "more" after a number ("24,544 more"). It is strongest when the content is trouble or uncertainty (problem, wrong, missing, going on) and weak on concrete nouns or plain declarative uses ("The train is going on to Paris", "The answer is", "missing my keys").

rival_explanations: Broader syntactic reading: the unit fires on any word that closes a wh- or relative-clause gap or an NP after a determiner, whatever its meaning, so 'what the plan is' or 'the thing I'm eating' would fire as strongly as problem phrasing.

Narrower topical reading: the unit is a help-forum troubleshooting detector ('what's going wrong', 'something I'm missing', 'how to fix it') and should stay near zero on academic abstract nouns like 'this observation' outside Q&A text.
Lexical reading: the unit fires on a fixed set of high-frequency closing tokens (' is', ' on', ' wrong', ' idea', ' more', ' nil') regardless of the clause structure around them.
